$comment: High/critical npm advisories accepted temporarily because NO patched release exists. Every entry needs a reason and an expiry date; scripts/audit-gate.mjs fails again after expiry. Policy: docs/security/README.md (npm audit exceptions).

advisories.reason: No patched node-forge release exists (vulnerable range covers every published version). It reaches the repo only through expo -> @expo/cli -> @expo/code-signing-certificates, i.e. Expo build tooling for expo-updates code signing, which OrenjiTrade does not use; the API (Java) and the web bundle do not include node-forge. npm's suggested fix downgrades Expo to SDK 44, which is not viable. Re-check when node-forge or @expo/cli publishes a fix.

No patched braces release exists (3.0.3 is the latest and is affected). braces is reached only through build/test tooling glob matching (micromatch via metro, jest, chokidar/fast-glob in the Angular and Expo toolchains); patterns are written by developers, never by users, and braces is not part of the web production bundle or the Java API. The DoS needs attacker-controlled, deeply nested brace patterns. Re-check when braces or micromatch publishes a fix.

The workspace's own zod is 4.6.6 (patched). The vulnerable copy is zod 3.25.76, which @expo/cli 57 requires (^3.25.76) and keeps in node_modules/@expo/cli/node_modules: no patched zod 3 release exists (the advisory's fix is 4.6.6 only), and forcing zod 4 on @expo/cli would break the Expo CLI, which imports the v3 API. It is Expo build and dev-server tooling: it is not in the app bundle, the Java API or the web bundle, and it validates the developer's own configuration, not user input. Re-check when @expo/cli moves to zod 4 or a patched zod 3 appears.

The only fixed release, decode-uri-component 0.5.1, is an ES module only; query-string 7.1.3, which expo-router 57 pins, loads it with require() and calls the default export, so an override would break the phone's router (Metro, Jest and Node interop return a module namespace, not the function). The latest query-string drops the dependency but is ESM only, and expo-router 57 requires query-string 7. The exposure is the phone client decoding its own route URLs and deep links (a quadratic slowdown on a crafted percent-encoded link): not in the web bundle (apps/web-angular does not use query-string) or the Java API. Re-check when expo-router moves off query-string 7 or a CommonJS fix appears.
